documents.excerpt: CITY OF LOS ANGELES INTER-DEPARTMENTAL MEMORANDUM Date:​ ​ July 31, 2026 To:​ ​ Honorable City Council c/o City Clerk, Room 395 Attention: Heather Hutt, Chair, Transportation Committee From:​ ​ Laura Rubio-Cornejo, General Manager ​ ​ Department of Transportation Subject:​ RESPONSE TO COUNCIL FILE 26-0251: I-110/GAFFEY STREET INCIDENT RESPONSE AND INFRASTRUCTURE COMMUNICATION PROTOCOLS SUMMARY On February 18, 2026, a fallen power pole caused a full closure of Interstate 110 near Gaffey Street in San Pedro. As directed in Council File (CF) 26‑0251, this report provides an overview of the Los Angeles Department of Transportation (LADOT) response and communication protocols during the I‑110/Gaffey Street incident. In compliance with CF 26‑0251, including a detailed timeline of the incident, an assessment of current electronic notification procedures, and an inventory of mobile traffic control devices used to support the department’s response. RECOMMENDATIONS That the City Council NOTE and FILE this report. BACKGROUND On February 18, 2026, a fallen power pole caused a full closure of Interstate 110 near Gaffey Street in San Pedro. In March 2026 the Los Angeles City Council (Council) requested the California Department of Transportation (Caltrans), Department of Transportation, and Department of Water and Power, in coordination with the Emergency Management Department, Los Angeles Police Department, and any other relevant agencies, to report with: A.​ A timeline of the response to the Interstate 110/Gaffey Street incident, including agency roles and communication protocols utilized. B.​ The availability, use, and protocols for electronic notifications to residents of similar road disruptions. C.​ The current inventory, location, and deployment status of portable changeable message signs and other mobile traffic control devices Citywide. Honorable City Council​ ​ ​ ​ ​ 2​ ​ ​ ​ July 31, 2026 D.​ Existing coordination protocols with Caltrans for incidents occurring on State freeway facilities within City boundaries, including delineation of responsibilities. E.​ Recommendations, if any, to improve resource availability, interagency coordination, and communication for residents for future incidents. This report provides an overview of LADOT’s response to the incident. DISCUSSION Operational and communication coordination between City and State agencies during such incidents is critical in mitigating impacts and keeping stakeholders informed. The deployment of portable traffic management equipment and interagency coordination protocols during such incidents is critical to ensure public safety, minimize congestion, and provide timely notice to motorists and nearby residents. This incident identified opportunities for enhanced coordination during inter-jurisdictional events in order to keep stakeholders, including local officials, responding agencies, and the public, better informed.
